Leave of Absence Administration Manual

Purpose
This manual describes how employees and managers should handle planned and unplanned leaves of absence, including medical leave, parental leave, bereavement leave, jury duty, and other protected or company-approved absences. The company is committed to supporting employees during significant life events while maintaining compliant documentation and consistent workflow across departments.

Types of Leave
Employees may be eligible for statutory or company-sponsored leave depending on work location, tenure, hours worked, and the nature of the request. Common categories include medical leave for the employee's serious health condition, family care leave, parental leave, bereavement leave, military-related leave, jury duty, and personal unpaid leave. Each category may have distinct notice requirements, certification rules, and pay treatment. HR determines the applicable leave type after reviewing the request and any supporting documentation.

Employee Responsibilities
Employees should notify their manager and HR as early as possible when a leave is anticipated. Planned leave requests must be submitted through the HRIS no fewer than 15 calendar days before the expected start date unless a shorter timeline is unavoidable. For emergency or unplanned leave, notice should be provided as soon as practical by phone, email, or the attendance hotline. Employees must supply accurate dates, expected duration, contact information, and any required certification forms. Failure to provide timely documentation may delay approval or result in the absence being tracked under a different leave category until review is complete.

Manager Responsibilities
Managers should acknowledge a leave notification on the same business day whenever possible and must not discourage employees from using protected leave. Managers are responsible for escalating the request to HR, maintaining confidentiality, identifying business coverage needs, and avoiding medical or legal interpretations on their own. Team leads should plan temporary task reassignment, customer communication ownership, and approval routing for work that would normally require the employee's attention.

HR Review and Approval Steps
HR reviews leave requests in five steps. First, confirm the request date, employee status, and location-specific eligibility criteria. Second, determine whether the leave appears protected by law or covered by company policy. Third, request certification or supporting documents, when applicable, and record deadlines for submission. Fourth, issue a written approval, provisional approval, or denial with explanation. Fifth, coordinate payroll coding, benefits handling, and return-to-work expectations with the employee and manager. All decisions must be documented in the HRIS case record.

Benefits and Pay Treatment
Paid leave categories are coded through payroll based on policy and legal requirements. Unpaid leave may affect benefit deductions, accruals, and holiday pay depending on duration and jurisdiction. HR and Payroll provide employees with a summary of any expected pay impacts before the leave begins whenever feasible. Employees remain responsible for any required benefit contributions during unpaid periods and should contact Payroll with repayment questions.

Return to Work
Before the employee returns, HR confirms the anticipated return date, any required release-to-work forms, and any workplace accommodations that need review. Managers must reinstate system access, update schedules, and provide a re-entry briefing on open priorities. If an employee cannot return on the expected date, the employee must inform HR immediately so the case can be reassessed.

Confidentiality and Compliance
Medical and sensitive personal records are stored separately from personnel files. Unauthorized disclosure, retaliation, or inconsistent leave handling may result in disciplinary action. Questions should be escalated to HR Business Partners or Legal when a leave request involves complex compliance issues.
